description: Whether to enable communication apps (Element).
label: Communication apps
name: apps.comms.enable

description: Whether to enable creative apps (GIMP, Inkscape, Krita, Penpot).
label: Creative apps
name: apps.creative.enable

description: Whether to enable developer tools (VSCodium, Nix toolchain, gcc).
label: Developer tools
name: apps.dev.enable

description: Whether to enable media player (VLC).
label: Media apps
name: apps.media.enable

description: Whether to enable office suite + mail (Thunderbird).
label: Office apps
name: apps.office.enable

description: Office suite installed when dawo.apps.office is enabled. Collabora resonates more with users coming from Windows.
label: Office suite
name: apps.office.suite

description: Password manager (KeePassXC). The one set that is opt-out: without a password manager people reuse passwords or write them down, so a deployment has to say no on purpose (e.g. it ships an organisation-wide vault).
label: Password manager and security apps
name: apps.security.enable

description: PipeWire audio (ALSA + PulseAudio compat). On by default; a host may disable it.
label: Audio
name: audio.enable

description:
Whether to enable desktop notifications on build/deploy events (comin's own user service).
Off by default: it also notifies at every graphical login, which is
noise on a device that updates cleanly. Turn it on where an update is
being watched
.
label: Tell the user about updates on the desktop
name: autoUpdate.desktopNotifications.enable

description: Whether to enable git-driven auto-update via comin.
label: Automatic updates
name: autoUpdate.enable

description: Poll interval in seconds (must be > 0).
label: Check interval (seconds)
name: autoUpdate.options.pollSeconds

description:
Say out loud that this deployment means to ship the password
documented in this module, and silence the warning about it.

The account exists so that somebody with no technical knowledge
ends up with a machine they can log into, which is worth keeping.
This option is how a deployment separates "we chose this" from
"nobody looked".
label: Keep the documented first password for the bootstrap account
name: bootstrapUser.acknowledgeDefaultPassword

description: Create the dawo bootstrap/break-glass admin. Set false once named admins (agenix) are in place.
label: Bootstrap admin account
name: bootstrapUser.enable

description:
Hash for the bootstrap account's first password, as `mkpasswd`
prints it. Empty falls back to the hash of the word written in this
module, which every reader of the repository knows.

It applies at account creation only (`mutableUsers = true`), so
changing it later does not reach a device that already exists.
label: First password of the bootstrap account (hash)
name: bootstrapUser.initialHashedPassword

description: Whether to enable authenticate to the release binary cache.
label: Cache authentication
name: cacheAuth.enable

description:
Hostname of the release cache. Must match the substituter's host
exactly: netrc is matched by machine name, and a mismatch is silent -
nix simply sends no credential and the device starts compiling.
label: Cache host
name: cacheAuth.host

description: Whether to enable GNOME desktop with GDM.
label: GNOME desktop
name: desktop.gnome.enable

description: Whether to enable KDE Plasma 6 desktop with SDDM.
label: KDE Plasma desktop
name: desktop.plasma.enable

description: Ship the Mastodon client (Tokodon). A deployment that does not want a social client sets this false.
label: Chat client
name: desktop.plasma.socialClient

description:
Unlock the KDE wallet with the login password, at the display manager.

Without this the wallet asks for a password of its own the first time
something wants a stored credential, which is the prompt people report
as "why does it ask again". NixOS wires kwallet into the `login` stack
by itself, but `login` is the tty; SDDM is where anyone actually
arrives at a desktop.

It only works when the wallet is named kdewallet and its password
equals the login password. A device whose wallet was created with a
different one keeps asking until that wallet is reset.
label: Unlock the KDE wallet at login
name: desktop.plasma.unlockWalletAtLogin

description: LUKS mapper name. The disko single-nvme-luks layout uses crypted-main.
label: LUKS mapper
name: diskUnlock.tpm2.device

description:
Whether to enable TPM2 auto-unlock of the LUKS root (PCR 7); passphrase kept as
break-glass. Requires a one-time on-device systemd-cryptenroll first
(see docs/secureboot-tpm.md).
label: TPM2 disk unlock
name: diskUnlock.tpm2.enable

description:
Expected hash of the archive. Null takes the hash nixpkgs itself
expects for the version it packages, which is the right answer
almost always: it moves with a nixpkgs bump instead of pinning this
fleet to whichever release happened to be current when someone wrote
it down.

Set it only to hold a specific archive deliberately, and expect to
revisit it when nixpkgs bumps the package.
label: DisplayLink driver hash
name: displaylink.driverHash

description:
Where to fetch the DisplayLink driver archive. Required when this
block is enabled, because the driver may not be redistributed here.

An organisation's own mirror is the better answer for a fleet: one
place to serve it from, no EULA click per device, and it keeps
working when the vendor moves its download. The vendor's direct link
works too. A `file://` path is accepted for a one-off machine.

The URL is not trusted - `driverHash` is. Whatever this points at
must hash to the value nixpkgs expects, or the build fails.
label: DisplayLink driver URL
name: displaylink.driverUrl

description: Whether to enable DisplayLink dock support (evdi + DisplayLink Manager).
label: DisplayLink dock support
name: displaylink.enable

description: Console base URL the request is sent to.
label: Console URL
name: elevationRequests.consoleUrl

description: Whether to enable let a user ask an operator for permission instead of needing the admin password.
label: Elevation requests
name: elevationRequests.enable

description:
How long the dialog waits for an answer. Matches the console's own
window; a device waiting longer would be sitting on a request the
server has already declared dead.
label: Wait (seconds)
name: elevationRequests.waitSeconds

description:
Spell check dictionaries installed for Firefox, by locale code.

The default is all eleven on offer - the ten most spoken languages in
Europe, with English in both its spellings - which costs about 26 MB
on every device. A deployment that knows its users only write two
languages should say so and carry only those.

The empty list installs none and leaves Firefox without spell
checking.
label: Firefox spelling dictionaries
name: firefox.dictionaries

description:
Norms this deployment claims. A rule tagged for one of them is on,
whatever the level says, because a norm asks for a set of rules
rather than for a degree of strictness.
label: Norms to comply with
name: hardening.compliance

label: Skip hardening rules with these tags
name: hardening.excludeTags

description:
How much of the register applies. Ordered: `baseline` is what every
device carries, `hardened` adds what a deployment opts into, and
`strict` adds what only a raised-risk device wants.

`none` selects nothing by level, which leaves the per-rule switches
and the compliance selection as the only way in.
label: Hardening level
name: hardening.level

description:
Per-rule override, and the reason this is a register rather than a
set of blocks. A rule set here wins over the level and over the
compliance selection, in both directions.
label: Per-rule hardening overrides
name: hardening.rules

description:
How often the device checks itself, as a systemd calendar
expression. The result goes to the journal so a fleet tool can read
it; empty turns the timer off and leaves the check on request and
after activation.
label: How often a device checks its own hardening
name: hardening.verifyOnCalendar

description: Allow device login over an unencrypted ldap:// directory. A simple bind carries the user's PASSWORD, so this turns on SSSD's own ldap_auth_disable_tls_never_use_in_production. Only for a directory that offers no TLS; the supported transport is ldaps:// (ADR 0021). Leave off unless you have accepted that risk in writing.
label: Onversleutelde directory-login toestaan
name: identity.allowPlaintextLdap

description: Service bind DN for SSSD (leave empty for anonymous bind).
label: Directory bind account
name: identity.bindDN

description: Secret-ref name of a file holding LDAP_BIND_PW=<password> (agenix, SSSD environmentFile).
label: Directory bind password
name: identity.bindSecret

description: Keep hashed credentials on the device so staff can sign in while offline (laptop on the road). Off forces a live directory bind for every login.
label: Offline login
name: identity.cacheCredentials

description: SSSD domain name.
label: Directory domain
name: identity.domain

description: Whether to enable directory-backed device login (SSSD).
label: Directory login
name: identity.enable

description: LDAP URI (identity/auth provider endpoint).
label: Directory address
name: identity.ldapUri

description: How many days a cached login stays valid without reaching the directory. After this, the device requires a live sign-in again.
label: Offline login validity (days)
name: identity.offlineLoginDays

description: Directory backend SSSD authenticates against. Vendor-neutral.
label: Directory type
name: identity.provider

description: LDAP search base.
label: Directory search base
name: identity.searchBase

description: PEM CA certificate chain for an ldaps:// directory signed by a private CA (public material, no secret). Empty = the system trust store (fine for Let's Encrypt-style certs).
label: Directory CA-certificaat (PEM)
name: identity.tlsCaCert

description: Whether to enable a local administrator account for when the directory is unreachable.
label: Local admin account
name: localAdmin.enable

description: Let each device draw its own password and hand it to the console, which shows it to an owner on the device page and can replace it there (design 0017). One password per device instead of one per scope, and none to keep anywhere else.
label: Password held by the console
name: localAdmin.managed

description: Secret-ref name of a file holding the password HASH (the output of `mkpasswd -m yescrypt`), not the password itself. Ignored when the console holds the password. Turning this integration off locks the account on every device, but does not delete it or its home directory.
label: Password (hash)
name: localAdmin.passwordSecret

description: Login name for the local administrator. Pick a name per organisation rather than reusing one across fleets: a shared name is a shared credential.
label: Username
name: localAdmin.username

description: Whether to enable join the self-hosted NetBird mesh.
label: NetBird mesh
name: netbird.enable

description: Self-hosted NetBird management server URL (sovereign; no SaaS).
label: NetBird management URL
name: netbird.managementUrl

description: Secret-ref name of the NetBird setup key (agenix). Reusable key enrolls the fleet.
label: NetBird setup key
name: netbird.setupKey

description: OpenBao API address as the DEVICE reaches it (mesh address once the routing peer is up).
label: Vault address
name: openbao.address

description: Whether to enable fetch device secrets from OpenBao (central vault).
label: OpenBao secrets
name: openbao.enable

description: KV v2 mount that holds the fleet's secrets.
label: Secrets mount
name: openbao.mount

description: Secret names to fetch. Each lands at /run/secrets/<name> and is linked from /run/agenix/<name> when agenix does not already provide it, so settings that reference a secret name keep working unchanged.
label: Secrets to fetch
name: openbao.secrets

description: Secret-ref name of the vault token file (agenix bootstrap for the experiment; device identity auth replaces it later).
label: Vault token
name: openbao.tokenSecret

description:
Failed attempts before the account locks. Low enough to stop
guessing, high enough to survive a keyboard layout somebody did
not expect.
label: Failed logins before an account locks
name: pam.lockout.attempts

description: Whether to enable lock an account after repeated failed logins.
label: Lock an account after repeated failed logins
name: pam.lockout.enable

description:
PAM services the lockout applies to. Every place a password can be
typed belongs here; a service left out is a way around it.
label: Logins that count towards the lockout
name: pam.lockout.services

description:
How long a lockout lasts. It expires on its own, on purpose: a
lock that only an administrator can lift turns a typo on a train
into a day without a laptop.
label: Seconds until a locked account unlocks
name: pam.lockout.unlockSeconds

description: Whether to enable require a password that is not trivially guessable.
label: Refuse easily guessed passwords
name: pam.quality.enable

description:
Minimum length. Length beats character classes: a long passphrase
somebody can remember is worth more than eight characters with a
symbol they wrote on a sticky note.
label: Minimum password length
name: pam.quality.minLength

description:
Whether to enable a hardware key (FIDO2) as a second factor for login and sudo. Off by
default and deliberately so: every user needs an enrolled key and a
recovery path before this is turned on, or it is a lockout with
extra steps. See docs/users.md
.
label: Require a security key at login
name: pam.u2f.enable

description:
Find printers announced on the local network automatically
(mDNS/IPP). Off means only printers configured centrally are
available - the right choice for a site that publishes its printers
from a server, and for a laptop that should not answer for printers
on whatever network it happens to be on.
label: Discover network printers
name: printing.discover

description:
Driver set. `open` covers the standard IPP Everywhere / PostScript
path most office printers speak. `broad` adds vendor driver packages
for older hardware, at the cost of a considerably larger system
closure on every device that has it.
label: Printer drivers
name: printing.drivers

description: Whether to enable printing (CUPS) on this device.
label: Printing
name: printing.enable

description: SANE scanning (driverless network + USB) + a scan frontend. On by default.
label: Scanning
name: scanning.enable

description: Whether to enable lanzaboote Secure Boot (requires sbctl keys enrolled at pkiBundle).
label: Secure Boot
name: secureboot.enable

description: Whether to enable hardened OpenSSH crypto + login policy (NCSC/CIS).
label: SSH access
name: ssh.enable

description: Max authentication attempts per connection (must be > 0).
label: Max authentication attempts
name: ssh.options.maxAuthTries

description: Whether to enable kernel/network sysctl baseline, strict sudo, temp-dir + login banner (BIO/NCSC).
label: Kernel hardening baseline
name: sysctlBaseline.enable

description: Whether to enable NTP time synchronization via chrony (BIO).
label: Time synchronisation
name: timesync.enable

description: NTP servers (must be non-empty). Override per organisation (e.g. an internal NTP).
label: NTP servers
name: timesync.options.servers

description: Whether to enable hardware/CLI diagnostics for ops/support (htop, lshw, pciutils, dmidecode, ethtool, lm_sensors, usbutils).
label: Diagnostic tools
name: tools.diagnostics.enable

description:
Hours during which this device may fetch and apply updates
(HH:MM-HH:MM, overnight ranges allowed). Empty means always.
label: Maintenance window
name: updates.maintenanceWindow

description: Whether to enable let ordinary users change desktop settings themselves.
label: User rights
name: userRights.enable

description:
Approve a Thunderbolt dock or device when it is plugged in. Without
this, a docked laptop silently does nothing until an administrator
visits it, which is the single most common first-day complaint about
a managed workstation.
label: Authorise a dock
name: userRights.options.docks

description:
Let a user apply firmware updates offered by fwupd. DOWNGRADES are
deliberately excluded: rolling firmware back to an older version is a
way to reinstate a fixed vulnerability, so it stays an administrator's
decision even where updating does not.
label: Install firmware updates
name: userRights.options.firmware

description:
Edit connections that apply to every user of the machine, including
VPN profiles the organisation ships. Separate from `wifi` on purpose:
joining a cafe network is a different act from rewriting the profile
that carries company traffic. Hostname and global DNS are deliberately
NOT included - those belong to the fleet, not to whoever is sitting at
the machine.
label: Change shared network profiles
name: userRights.options.networkProfiles

description:
Add, remove and configure printers. Needs `dawo.printing` to be on -
without CUPS there is nothing to authorise. Job control for other
people's jobs is not included; this is about a user connecting the
printer in front of them.
label: Add and manage printers
name: userRights.options.printers

description:
Mount removable drives and memory cards. Mounting devices the system
itself owns (an internal disk, anything in fstab) stays with the
administrator, so this cannot be used to reach a partition the user
was not meant to see. Note that USB device control, if enabled, still
decides whether the drive is allowed to appear at all - that is a
separate and earlier question.
label: Mount USB storage
name: userRights.options.removableMedia

description:
Set the time zone when travelling. Setting the CLOCK itself is not
included and should not be: time comes from the fleet's NTP servers,
and a machine whose user can move the clock can move it past a
certificate expiry or muddle every log timestamp on it.
label: Change the time zone
name: userRights.options.timezone

description:
Turn WiFi on or off, scan, and connect to a network, saving it for
this user. Does not include company-wide connection profiles - those
are `networkProfiles`. This is what a laptop needs to work anywhere
other than the desk it was imaged on.
label: Choose a network
name: userRights.options.wifi

description: Wazuh agent group (server-side policy grouping).
label: Wazuh agent group
name: wazuh.agentGroup

description: Whether to enable report to a Wazuh manager (endpoint security agent).
label: Endpoint security (Wazuh)
name: wazuh.enable

description: Secret-ref name of the Wazuh enrollment password (agenix; agent-auth registers with it).
label: Wazuh enrolment secret
name: wazuh.enrollmentSecret

description: Wazuh manager address the agent reports to.
label: Wazuh manager
name: wazuh.manager

description: Whether to enable Zsh as an interactive shell (opt-in).
label: Zsh shell
name: zsh.enable
